why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` maps to the real script `node --test`, which picks up test/strutil.test.js. All the node one-liners use `--input-type=module -e` with double-quoted bash and JS strings in single quotes, and none of them contain `$` or backticks. In the README check, bash turns `\\\\b` inside double quotes into `\\b`, which the JS string turns into a regex `\b`, so the word-boundary test is valid. The imports from './index.js', 'node:fs' and 'node:assert/strict' are valid when run from the repo root. `echo exit=$?` sits outside the quotes, so it runs correctly. The only hazard is `!new` inside double quotes, which would trigger history expansion in an interactive bash, but agents run non-interactive shells where that is off. Every file named (index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js) exists at this commit, and the arguments fit each program.
